samples.summary: Backslash-escaping test omits the actual injection vector it documents (backslash immediately before a quote)
samples.evidence: The new test only feeds a lone trailing backslash (`'a\\'` in TS = `a\`) and asserts `document_id = 'a\\'`. The comment above it, and the doc comment on `sql()` (analytics-warehouse.service.ts:35-39), describe the danger as `a\'` — a backslash that escapes the following quote — and justify the ORDER of the two `.replace()` calls. No test exercises a value containing both a backslash and a quote (e.g. `a\'b OR 1=1--`), so the ordering/interaction the comment claims to protect is not covered: a future refactor that swaps or drops the interaction would still pass. The lone-backslash case is a real regression test (it fails pre-fix), so this is a coverage gap rather than fake coverage.
searchedFor: grep for `sql(` / escape tests in packages/backend/src/analytics

finding.summary: New 403-specific error message in DocumentAnalyticsPage has no test
finding.evidence: The diff adds a distinct rendering branch: `error instanceof HttpError && error.status === 403` renders a permission-specific message instead of "Failed to load analytics." No test exercises either branch. There is no test file for document-analytics.tsx (globbed packages/frontend/src/app/analytics/** — only date-range.test.ts, format.test.ts, series.test.ts, views-trend-chart.test.tsx exist), and the new test added by this PR (packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/__tests__/workspace-analytics.test.tsx) covers only the ranking page. So nothing verifies that getDocumentAnalytics actually surfaces an `HttpError` instance with `.status === 403` through react-query (it goes through `assertOk` in api/http-error.ts and `fetchWithAuth`); if the thrown error were wrapped or a different class, the page would silently keep showing the generic text and every suite would still be green.

verdict.reason: The finding claims there is no test file for document-analytics.tsx and that neither error branch is exercised. Both claims are false. packages/frontend/src/app/analytics/document-analytics.test.tsx exists and renders the real DocumentAnalyticsPage with the real HttpError class inside a real QueryClientProvider/MemoryRouter, covering: (1) HttpError 403 -> asserts the permission message renders AND that "failed to load analytics" is absent (test.tsx:40-49); (2) HttpError 500 -> asserts generic message AND that the permission text is absent (:51-60), which is precisely the assertion that would catch an over-broad instanceof check; (3) plain Error -> generic fallback (:62-68). These are two-sided, non-vacuous assertions that fail if the branch at document-analytics.tsx:60 is removed or inverted. The reviewer's fallback over-mocking concern also does not hold under this lens: only the network boundary is mocked, while the branch logic, HttpError class, and react-query error propagation are real; and the chain is unconditional — getDocumentAnalytics calls assertOk (api/analytics.ts:129), which always throws HttpError carrying response.status (api/http-error.ts:116,120), with no wrapping path to a different class. The reviewer's own stated Glob would have listed this test file, so the enumerated evidence is inaccurate.
